Status.note:
Status:
- Open the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx and go to the Operating sheet. Plant 64020, West Riverside Energy Center, lists generators CTG3, CTG4 and STG2 as '(OP) Operating', all with operating month 5 and year 2020. No planned retirement year is shown, and the plant does not appear on the Planned, Retired or Canceled or Postponed sheets.
- I found no retirement, mothballing or change of status. The owners' 2023 filing at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=481060 also calls the plant in service since May 14, 2020.
- The Public Service Commission docket 6680-CE-192 filed in March 2026 is about the older Riverside Energy Center Units 1 and 2 (EIA plant 55641, generators CTG1 and CTG2), not this combined cycle unit.

milestones.note: EIA-860M Operating sheet shows operating month 5, year 2020 for CTG3, CTG4 and STG2

Backup Power.note:
Backup Power:
- Open the Alliant Energy press release from May 15, 2020 at https://www.globenewswire.com/en/news-release/2020/05/15/2034386/0/en/Alliant-Energy-s-West-Riverside-Energy-Center-goes-into-service.html. The sub-headline reads 'New natural gas generating station is now providing power to Wisconsin customers'. That describes routine power for the grid, not a backup engine set.
- No document uses the words backup power for this plant. So the value stays no. The release implies it rather than stating it.

units.notes: The unit is still operating in the EIA table for September 2026. No retirement or ownership change was found. Backup Power stays no, supported only by an implied source.

Owner(s).value: Wisconsin Power and Light Co [57%]; Wisconsin Electric Power Co [27%]; MGE Energy Inc [7%]; small shareholder(s) [9%]
Owner(s).note:
Owners:
- The database lists six owners. Our rules record the four largest and fold the rest into one line, and owners under 5 percent are grouped as small shareholders. So I shortened the list to Wisconsin Power and Light, Wisconsin Electric Power, MGE Energy and small shareholders.
- Open the joint application to the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin filed October 2, 2023 (docket 5-AE-245) at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=481060. On page 7, the table just below the paragraph that starts 'Together, the units have a nameplate capacity of 727.2 MW' lists current ownership: Wisconsin Power and Light 412.2 MW at 56.6 percent, Wisconsin Electric 200 MW at 27.5 percent, MGE 50 MW at 6.9 percent, Adams-Columbia Electric Cooperative 32.6 MW at 4.5 percent, Rock Energy Cooperative 26.9 MW at 3.7 percent and Central Wisconsin Electric Cooperative 5.5 MW at 0.8 percent.
- The three cooperatives are each under 5 percent and add up to 9.0 percent, which is the small shareholder line. I rounded 27.5 percent down to 27 so the shares total 100.
- The Alliant Energy quarterly report for September 30, 2024 is gone from its old address at energycentral.com. A saved copy is cited instead at https://web.archive.org/web/20250307014442/https://energycentral.com/news/alliant-energy-corporation-quarterly-report-quarter-ending-september-30-2024-form-10-q . In its notes to the financial statements it says 'WPL's undivided current ownership interest in West Riverside is 56.6%', which matches. The old address is kept in the source box, because sources are never removed.
- The 2023 transfer in that docket was a proposal, so I did not change any share for it.
